title: CLO 2025.1 - Seamless Partitioning

chunks.content: # CLO 2025.1 - Seamless Partitioning This document explains the Seamless Partitioning feature in CLO 2025.1, focusing on how to create and manipulate seamless division lines for fabric design. It covers technical procedures, tools, fabric application, and the advantages of this function in pattern modification and simulation. --- ## Introduction to Seamless Partitioning Seamless Partitioning in CLO 2025.1 allows designers to separate fabric areas without cutting and sewing sheets. Traditionally, flat color designs required cutting fabric sheets and setting them separately. With seamless division, each area can be separated and assigned different colors, textures, or materials, such as needles or appliqués, without physical cutting. This feature is especially useful for designs combining various colors or materials. --- ## Creating Seamless Division Lines ### Location and Basic Usage - The Seamless Division tool is located under the Multi-Edged Tool in the 2D toolbar. - To create a seamless division line, start by pressing on the outside line of the fabric board. Starting inside the board is not allowed. - The line can be drawn similarly to inner lines by clicking multiple points to form any shape. - Holding the Shift key restricts line drawing to 45-degree angles, aiding precision. - To finish drawing, double-click outside the board. ### Symmetry Support - If the board has symmetrical links (one or two axes), lines created on one side auto-duplicate on the other. - This suits boards with symmetrical axes. - For asymmetrical designs, lines can be created on only one side without duplication. ### Visual Representation - In the 2D window, seamless division lines appear highlighted in light blue. - In the 3D clothing view, they appear as dark red lines, visually identical to inner lines. --- ## Editing Seamless Division Lines ### Adjusting Lines - Use the Edit Board tool to modify endpoints or line segments. - Both straight lines and curves can be edited. - Curved lines are created by clicking and dragging to add Bezier curve handles. - Holding Ctrl while dragging creates curve points, allowing free curve shaping. - Mistakes can be corrected by deleting points with the Delete key. ### Non-Divisional Curves - After creating division lines, create non-divisional curves along the outside of the board or existing non-divisional curves. - Non-divisional curves must always start from a closed shape. - These curves can be edited or deleted using the Edit Board tool. - Internal or basic lines can be converted to non-divisional curves by selecting the loop outline tool, right-clicking the line, and choosing "Non-Divisional Curve" from the menu. - This conversion avoids redrawing lines and helps finalize designs. ### Batch Creation of Non-Divisional Curves - Right-click on a non-divisional curve and select "Non-Divisional Curve Frame" to open a dialog. - This dialog allows input of the number and distance of multiple non-divisional curves. - Useful for pattern design, division, and repetitive materials.

chunks.content: - Internal or basic lines can be converted to non-divisional curves by selecting the loop outline tool, right-clicking the line, and choosing "Non-Divisional Curve" from the menu. - This conversion avoids redrawing lines and helps finalize designs. ### Batch Creation of Non-Divisional Curves - Right-click on a non-divisional curve and select "Non-Divisional Curve Frame" to open a dialog. - This dialog allows input of the number and distance of multiple non-divisional curves. - Useful for pattern design, division, and repetitive materials. --- ## Applying Fabrics to Seamless Divisions - Fabrics can be applied to separated areas by dragging the desired fabric from the Object window to either the 2D or 3D window. - Even in symmetrical boards, fabric application is independent per area; simultaneous fabric application to symmetrical areas does not occur. - This allows greater design flexibility. - The Adjustment Board tool can also be used to select areas and assign fabric. --- ## Pattern Adjustment and Simulation with Seamless Partitioning - Use the Edit Pattern tool to adjust fabric patterns on separated areas, such as pants. - The physical properties of fabrics are applied according to the non-divisional curves, allowing simulation of different fabric behaviors in one garment. - A critical advantage is that when the paper pattern is modified, the non-divisional curve lines automatically adjust proportionally, preserving the design intent. - This is particularly convenient during frequent design modifications as it reduces the need to manually edit inner lines. ### Extension and Subtraction Functions - The non-divisional curve line supports extension or subtraction functions to maintain original extension directions after pattern modifications. - This feature can be toggled on or off based on design needs. --- ## Additional Features of Seamless Partitioning ### Sticker Application - Stickers can be added on or near the front seamless curve without affecting their display. - Stickers appear natural, as if no division line exists. ### Seam Parameters - Seamless curve lines can be assigned specific parameters similar to internal lines. - Seams can be added as required to the seamless curve. ### Display and Compatibility Notes - Areas with seamless partitioning are not displayed in the Hard Nuvos window. - When opening files from CLO 2025.1 in previous versions, seamless curve lines revert to basic lines. - Remember to set coats to the entire panel when adding a seamless curve line to ensure correct fabric behavior. --- ## Summary Seamless Partitioning in CLO 2025.1 enables advanced fabric area separation without physical cutting, supporting complex color and material designs. It integrates smoothly with pattern editing and simulation workflows, enhancing design flexibility and efficiency. Understanding the creation, editing, fabric application, and simulation processes enables designers to fully utilize this feature for creative and precise garment design.
